questions.cardText:
[Archaeology] What is the oldest still-standing structure made by humans?
A. The Great Pyramid of Giza
B. The Megalithic Temples of Malta
C. Göbekli Tepe
Answer: C. Göbekli Tepe dates back to a time close to the end of the last Ice Age when woolly mammoths were still roaming parts of the Earth.
questions.de: Welche jungsteinzeitliche Stätte im Südosten der Türkei, um 9500 v. Chr. gegen Ende der letzten Eiszeit erbaut, besitzt Steinpfeiler, die zu den ältesten bekannten Megalithen der Welt zählen?
questions.en: Which Neolithic site in south-eastern Turkey, built around 9500 BC near the end of the last Ice Age, holds stone pillars that are among the world's oldest known megaliths?

timeline.labelEn: Göbekli Tepe in Upper Mesopotamia is built, with some of the world's oldest known megaliths
timeline.labelDe: Göbekli Tepe in Obermesopotamien wird errichtet, mit einigen der ältesten bekannten Megalithen der Welt

questions.notes: 'Oldest still-standing structure made by humans' is a loose superlative (the site was deliberately buried, and claims vary); Wikipedia calls its pillars 'among the world's oldest known megaliths'. Reworked to that.

questions.cardText:
[Earth Science] If you could drive straight up from the Earth’s surface at highway speeds, how long would it take to reach space?
A. About 1 hour
B. About 10 hours
C. About 100 hours
Answer: A. The Kármán line, located at an altitude of about 62 miles (100 kilometers), is commonly used to define the boundary between Earth’s atmosphere and outer space.
questions.de: In welcher Höhe liegt die Kármán-Linie, die gängige Grenze zum Weltraum, die man bei Autobahntempo senkrecht nach oben in etwa einer Stunde erreichen würde?
questions.en: At what altitude lies the Kármán line, commonly used as the boundary of space, so that driving straight up at highway speed would reach it in about an hour?

timeline.labelEn: The FAI establishes the Kármán line at 100 km as the boundary between aeronautics and astronautics
timeline.labelDe: Die FAI legt die Kármán-Linie in 100 km Höhe als Grenze zwischen Luft- und Raumfahrt fest

questions.notes: Card's answer (about 1 hour) checks out: 100 km at ~100 km/h (62 mi at ~60 mph). The 100 km line is widely but not universally accepted (the US uses 50 miles).
